reviewer: Separate Claude review agent, independent of the collector and extractor; no human review claimed
scope: Independent review of the rare-disease candidate ranking batch for use-case-rare-disease-candidate-ranking: 616 records (496 results, 56 evaluations, 27 configurations, 10 claims of which 7 are relevance judgements, 9 methods, 7 protocols, 6 datasets, 4 sources, 1 model). All four pinned artifacts were re-downloaded and matched their recorded SHA-256. All 496 results were re-read from the pinned cells with a separate parser (the extractor's script was not run) and match in printed and numeric value, locator, metric, qualifier, unit, direction, evaluation, configuration, protocol and dataset; every top-k row is monotone and every percentage is a whole number of cases over the cohort size. The 7 judgements are source_checked with reviewed_evaluations (one changed from direct to proxy); pins are not set. Corrections change no number and are listed in docs/reviews/use-cases/rare-disease-candidate-ranking-2026-10-09.md.
limitations: Automated review by a Claude agent; not human scientific review, not reproduction of any tool or model and not clinical validation.
The sources print rates only, so no rate could be recomputed from counts; whole-number consistency with the cohort size was checked instead.
Figures were not read (Yuan et al. 2024 Figure 2 option tables; Yuan et al. 2022 Supplementary Figure 2).
Yuan et al. 2022 SM Tables 1, 2 and 4 and Kafkas et al. Supplementary Tables S5 and S6 were not opened.
Europe PMC supplementaryFiles zips are assembled per request; only the SM Table 3 docx member hash can be re-verified.
Pins for the 7 judgements are not set; the use case's assessed_by links and gaps are approved in the dated review but not applied here.
npm run build was not run, by instruction. npm test and npm run typecheck passed, and a scratch-store dry run of addBatch, loadRecords and deriveUseCaseInputs succeeded.
Rerunning extract/extract_rare_ranking.py would restore the collector's wording for the corrected fields.

errors.message: comparison.inputs said trio mode not stated; Discussion paragraph 1 item 4 says AMELIE ran only in singleton mode and LIRICAL trio mode was under development. Now singleton.
Origin was independent_paper; the evaluated system is GPT-4 with prompts the authors designed, so author_reported.

Limitations corrected: mode per row, in-sample tuning narrowed to the chosen protocols, figure-only option sets, authorship of the prompts, unstated zero-shot prompt, random-gene pool, best-baseline selection, GPCards prompt development.
Locator was Discussion paragraph 1; the text is Discussions paragraph 3. Value now notes the top-20 detail and that the subset result is in Supplementary Figure 2 only.
Population descriptions completed from the source (KMCGD mixed syndromes, 2.0 HPO terms; GPCards 50 variants and used for prompt development).
Relevance changed from direct to proxy: the cohort is a mixed clinical-genetics population, not the defined congenital-anomaly or developmental-disorder population in the use case setting.
Archived article contained Table 2 (one row per case with causal variant) and case IDs in prose. Removed; URL and SHA-256 remain on the source record.
